newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium could envisage help for new Congo military.
newsitem.headline: Belgium could envisage help for new Congo military.

text.p: Belgium Defence Minister Jean-Pol Poncelet said on Wednesday he could envisage resuming military cooperation with the Democratic Republic of the Congo, formerly Zaire.

"In the perspective of a resumption of official (Belgian) cooperation with the Congo, according to the conditions fixed by the (Belgian) government, I am disposed to respond favourably to an eventual request for cooperation coming from the new Congolese authorities," the Belgian news agency Belga quoted Poncelet as saying.
He was speaking to an association of graduates of Belgium's Royal Military School.

Belgium cut official aid to Zaire, its former colony, in 1990 over charges that Zairean troops had killed students at Lubumbashi University who protested against the regime of President Mobutu Sese Sekko.

After rebels led by Laurent Kabila ousted Mobutu in May, Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said Belgium was ready to cooperate with the new regime, but only when certain conditions were met - notably progress towards democracy.
Poncelet was quoted as saying a resumption of military cooperation between the two countries could aim to contribute to army training on the ground and in Belgium.

Such a contribution could help the transition to democracy and the peaceful development of the country being led from now on by Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL), he said.
"I continue to think that Belgium can play a role vis-a-vis this region of Africa, even if the modes will no longer be the same as in the past," he added.
